newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Tanzania to repatriate ex-Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania to repatriate ex-Zaire refugees.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania said they had agreed on the repatriation of 90,000 refugees from the ex-Zaire currently on Tanzanian soil.
A joint statement on the accord was issued after talks in Kinshasa on Sunday between Tanzanian leader Benjamin Mkapa, ending a two-day visit, and host President Laurent Kabila.

"The government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expressed its commitment and readiness to receive all her refugees so that they come back and contribute to the reconstruction and development of their country," Kabila's Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha said.

"The relevant Congolese and Tanzanian authorities were therefore directed to faciliate with immediate effect the voluntary repatriation of refugees currently residing in Tanzania in coordination with the UNHCR (United Nations refugee agency)," Kahara said, reading from the statement.
The refugees fled Democratic Congo -- then known as Zaire -- last year in the early stages of Kabila's armed campaign to overthrow veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko.
The war started in the vast country's eastern border provinces, not far from Tanzania. Thousands of refugees flooded across Lake Tanganyika which straddles the two countries.
Kabila entered Kinshasa in mid-May after Mobutu fled and decreed himself president of the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.

At a joint news conference, Kabila repeated that his government was ready to cooperate with a U.N. investigation into charges that his forces massacred Rwandan Hutu refugees during his seven-month guerrilla drive across the vast country.
"We're waiting for the U.N. investigators," Kabila said. "We accepted to cooperate with the investigation a long time ago. We remain quite willing to receive the U.N. team at any time."
Kabila has repeatedly denied the charges.
The two heads of state, in their joint statement, deplored the "vilification campaign" against Democratic Congo.
